questions.question: Bramho Samaj was founded by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bramho Samaj **was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in **1828.**
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a **social reformer** who advocated for the **abolition of Sati **and worked towards the** upliftment of women in society.**
 
• Bramho Samaj was a **socio-religious movement **that aimed to promote **monotheism and rationalism in Hinduism.**
 
• The movement also advocated for the **eradication of caste system** and encouraged education and social reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keshab Chandra Sen **was a disciple of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and played a significant role in the growth of **Bramho Samaj.**
 
• **Debendranath Tagore **was also a disciple of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and his** son-in-law,** who later became the leader of the Bramho Samaj movement.
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati **was the founder of **Arya Samaj,** another socio-religious movement in India that aimed to promote **Vedic teachings and eradicate social evils.**

questions.question: Which Kushana ruler was famous in history as a great patron of Buddhism and organised the fourth Buddhist Council?

• The **fourth Buddhist Council **was held in Kashmir during the reign of Kanishka, which was attended by Buddhist scholars and monks from across the region.
 
• He was one of the most famous and influential Kushana rulers who ruled from 127 CE to 150 CE.
 
• He is known for his patronage of Buddhism and organizing the fourth Buddhist Council, which was attended by scholars and monks from across the region.
 
• Kanishka also built several Buddhist stupas and monasteries, which helped spread the religion throughout his empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vasudeva I:**

 
 
• He was a Kushana ruler who **succeeded Kanishka. **
 
• He is known for his** military campaigns** and expanding the Kushana empire, but there is no evidence to suggest that he was a patron of Buddhism or organized any Buddhist councils.
 
 
 
• **Vima Kadphises:**
 
 
• He was one of the early Kushana rulers who **succeeded Kujula Kadphises.**
 
• He is known for his **military campaigns** and expanding the Kushana empire, but there is no evidence to suggest that he was a patron of Buddhism or organized any Buddhist councils.
 
 
 
• **Huvishka: **
 
 
• **​**He was a Kushana ruler who **succeeded Kanishka** and ruled from **150 CE to 180 CE**.
 
• He continued the **patronage of Buddhism **and built several Buddhist stupas and monasteries, but there is no evidence to suggest that he organized any Buddhist councils.

questions.question: Why can you not see objects in a dim lit room when you come from a brightly lit room?

options.text: The iris dilates the eye lens to allow less light to enter the eye.
The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
The vitreous humour dilates the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
The cornea contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When we move from a** brightly lit room to a dimly lit room,** our eyes take some time to **adjust** to the change in lighting.
 
• This is because the** iris**, which controls the amount of light entering the eye, needs to** adjust to the new** lighting conditions.
 
• This helps to improve the **clarity of the image** that is formed on the retina.
 
• Dilation of the eye lens actually allows more** light to enter the eye**, and so this would not help in a dimly lit room.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iris:**

 
 
• The iris is a** circular muscle** in the eye that **controls the size **of the pupil and the **amount of light entering** the eye.
 
• It is responsible for adjusting the amount of light that enters the eye based on the** lighting conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Pupil: **
 
 
• **​**The pupil is the **black circular opening **in the center of the iris that allows light to enter the eye.
 
• Its size is **controlled by the iris**, which adjusts it based on the amount of light available.
 
 
 
• **Vitreous humour:**
 
 
• The vitreous humour is a **gel-like substance t**hat fills the eye and helps to maintain its shape.
 
• It does** not have any control** over the amount of light entering the eye.
 
 
 
• **Cornea:**
 
 
• The cornea is a **transparent layer** at the front of the eye that helps to focus light onto the retina.
 
• It does not have any control over the amount of** light entering the eye.**

questions.question: Which of the following is found in plant cells only?

• It is a** thin, flexible barrier** made up of **lipids and proteins** that surrounds the cell and regulates the movement of materials in and out of the cell.
 
 
 
• **Nucleolus:**
 
 
• It is a **dense, spherical structure** found within the nucleus of eukaryotic cells, which is involved in the synthesis of **ribosomal RNA** and the assembly of ribosomes.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• These are **membrane-bound organelles** found in **eukaryotic cells**, which are responsible for producing energy in the form of **ATP through cellular respiration**.
 
• They contain their** own DNA** and can replicate independently within the cell.

questions.question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before _______.

options.text: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
the Chief Minister of the concerned state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor of an Indian state** is appointed by the** President of India** and holds the office during the** pleasure of the President.**
 
• Before entering upon his office, the Governor takes an** oath or affirmation** before the** Chief Justice of the High Court** exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State.
 
• The purpose of taking the oath or affirmation is to ensure that the Governor will **faithfully discharge the duties **of his office and uphold the **Constitution and the laws** of the land.
 
• The oath or affirmation is a solemn promise made by the Governor to fulfill his** obligations with honesty, integrity, and dedication.**
 
• The Chief Justice of the High Court administering the oath or affirmation is a symbol of the** independence of the judiciary** and the **rule of law.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** President **is the **appointing authority of the Governor on the recommendation of Council of Ministers** and does not administer the oath or affirmation.
 
• The **Chief Minister **is the **head of the state government** and has no role in the appointment or swearing-in of the Governor.
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the** head of the central government **and has no role in the appointment or swearing-in of the Governor.

questions.question:
The given equation provides the property of the motion of an object, traversing a circular path. What is ‘v’ in this equation?

ac = v²/R
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The equation** ac = v²/R** provides the **centripetal acceleration** of an object moving in a **circular path.**
 
• Here, 'v' represents the **speed or velocity** of the object.
 
• The unit of speed is** meters per second** (m/s) or **kilometers per hour** (km/h).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distance** is the** total length **covered by an object in motion and is measured in** meters (m) or kilometers (km).**
 
• **Surface area **is the total area occupied by the** surface of an object **and is measured in **square units **like square meters (m²) or square centimeters (cm²).
 
• **Intensity **is the measure of the** strength or power **of a phenomenon such as light, sound, or radiation and is measured in units like** watts per square meter (W/m²) or decibels (dB).**

questions.question: The term of trade refers to ______.

options.text: the excess of import expenditures over export earnings
the terms and conditions on which a country is offered loan
the ratio between export prices and import prices

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the ratio between export prices and import prices.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **term of trade** is the ratio between the** prices of a country's exports** and the** prices of its imports.**
 
• It is an indicator of a **country's economic performance** in international trade.
 
• If the ratio improves, it means that a country can** buy more imports **with the same quantity of exports, which is favorable for its economy.
 
• In contrast, if the** ratio deteriorates**, it means that a country needs to** export more** to buy the same quantity of imports, which can be a challenge for its economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade agreements** are **not** the same as the term of trade, although they can affect it by **influencing the demand** for a country's exports or imports.
 
• **Loan conditions** are** not** related to the term of trade, although they can affect a **country's ability to pay** for its imports or to invest in its exports.

questions.question: ______ of the Constitution of India says that the State shall take steps to organise panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self - government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 40 **of the Constitution of India mandates the State to take necessary measures to** organize Panchayats **and endow them with powers and authority to function as **self-governing units.**
 
• This article is a part of** Directive Principles of State Policy**, which are non-justiciable in nature but are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The objective behind this article is to promote** democratic decentralization** and **grassroots-level democracy** in India.
 
• Panchayats are an essential institution of **local self-government** in rural areas, and the Constitution recognizes their significance in the **development** of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 35** of the Indian Constitution gives** Parliament** the power to make laws that implement the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution.
 
• **Article 38** pertains to the State's duty to secure a **social order** for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
 
• **Article 32** provides for the** right to constitutional remedies** for enforcing fundamental rights.
